issues.description: New command names break the established singular-dash naming convention used by sibling commands.
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark-add, quickmark-save, bookmark-add, bookmark-load (singular, hyphenated). The patch adds quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload, exposed as :quickmarks-reload / :bookmarks-reload. This breaks discoverability and forces users to remember two conventions. Rename to quickmark-reload / bookmark-reload and update the feature file accordingly.

issues.description: reload() clears state before parsing, leaving the manager half-populated if parsing fails.
issues.detail: The method calls self.marks.clear() then parses; if _parse_line raises (InvalidUrlError, etc.), marks are partially populated and changed has already been emitted. The contract should be parse-then-swap, or the partial-failure behavior must be documented. Also note reload() now fires changed from __init__, weakening the signal's post-init-mutation contract.

issues.description: Unit test does not cover removal semantics — only one entry replaced by another.
issues.detail: test_reload rewrites a single URL. The load-bearing line is self.marks.clear(), so the test should verify that entries present at construction but absent on disk at reload time are dropped, and that duplicates aren't double-added. A multi-entry before/after disjoint set would pin the contract.

issues.description: New BDD scenarios are unnamed, breaking the feature file's voice.
issues.detail: Both new scenarios are bare `Scenario:` with no title, while every other scenario in the file has a descriptive name like 'Saving a quickmark'. Test names are part of the spec and keep output greppable. Add names such as 'Reloading bookmarks from disk'.

issues.description: reload() docstring omits pre/postconditions and the discard-unsaved-state behavior.
issues.detail: The docstring says 'Reload quickmarks/bookmarks from disk' but doesn't state the contract: discards current marks (including unsaved in-memory changes), repopulates from the backing file, and emits changed on completion. Documenting this prevents the next maintainer from being surprised by silent data loss when a save is in flight.

issues.description: Two near-identical command bodies invite a tiny helper.
issues.detail: quickmarks_reload and bookmarks_reload are six lines each, identical except for the registry key and message string. A small private helper _reload_marks(name, label) would collapse both to one line and make the duplication explicit. Optional cleanup, but the shape is obvious.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the refactor extracting reload() onto UrlMarkManager is the right shape — one code path for loading, shared by construction and on-demand reload. Two issues block landing as-is: the new command names break the codebase's singular-dash convention (quickmark-* / bookmark-*), and reload() clears state before parsing, so a parse failure leaves the manager half-populated with changed already emitted. Secondary cleanups: unit tests don't cover removal semantics, the new BDD scenarios are unnamed, and the docstring should document the discard-unsaved-state contract. Fix naming, parse-then-swap, tighten tests and docs — then land.
